 Evander rises to the occasion in FC Cincinnati's Wild Card win
 Ben Wright
 Copy URL 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on X 
 FC Cincinnati 's biggest star helped deliver their biggest win of the season on Thursday.
 Evander scored a brace and added an assist as the Orange & Blue (No. 9) rallied for a  3-1 win at Orlando City (No. 8) in the Eastern Conference Wild Card. They'll face Supporters' Shield champions Nashville SC in Round One of the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs.
 "We showed tonight that we don't want to finish the season here," the Brazilian No. 10 said after scoring his first career playoff goals at Inter.co Stadium. 
 "I think the mentality was there and the way that we managed the game, even though starting the game behind in the score. It was great."
 Goal number 2 for Evander! 💪
That's a brace for the MVP finalist and @fccincinnati takes the lead // Audi MLS Cup Playoffs pic.twitter.com/ThVwVRPIOi 
— Major League Soccer (@MLS) November 20, 2026 
 Brazilian maestro steps up
 After going down a goal to Martín Ojeda 's 26th-minute opener, Cincinnati were up against it, consistently under pressure in the midst of a Florida downpour. 
 However, Evander's penalty kick on the brink of halftime and rebound finish following a slick team passing move just after the break gave the visitors the lead in the 50th minute. 
 They never relinquished it, withstanding a barrage of Orlando attacks before Samuel Gidi iced the game with five minutes remaining. 
 "I think we understood what it would take to win this game," added Evander, a two-time Best XI midfielder who notched his first three playoff goal contributions (2g/1a) on Thursday. 
 "It was a great game from everybody. We had to suffer, we knew how to handle the pressure as well, and I think we deserved the win."
 This one was for Fiona. 🧡 pic.twitter.com/Vigul0kziG 
— FC Cincinnati (@fccincinnati) November 20, 2026 
 On to Nashville
 Things won't get any easier for Evander & Co., who'll face a historic Nashville side in Round One, beginning with Sunday's opener at GEODIS Park (4 pm ET | Apple TV ; FS1, FOX Deportes).
 The Coyotes easily took the regular-season series, winning both games by a combined 6-0 scoreline. That includes a  2-0 Nashville win at Cincy's TQL Stadium on Decision Day.
 "There’s been a lot of pressure on us throughout the whole season because, to be honest, we haven’t had a good season," said Evander. "And this is the time to change. I just told the boys to come out and enjoy the night. I think we need to enjoy the next upcoming games and try to save the season.
 "If we play like we played tonight, we can make it to the final.”
